ai.description: This small gecko reaches 40 mm SVL. It is pale brown with a distinct dark, net-like reticulation on the back. Key features include subdigital lamellae and a series of small, uniform dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus reticulatus* is uniquely identified by the distinct, dark, net-like reticulated pattern on its back, which contrasts sharply with the plain or spotted dorsum of other Indian *Hemidactylus* species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus reticulatus* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands across the Indian peninsula, typically found at low to moderate elevations on trees and rocky outcrops.
ai.behavior: The Reticulate Leaf-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt small insects on tree trunks and rocky surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus reticulatus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of one or two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus reticulatus* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh at low elevations.
